summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes and bilateral below-knee amputations was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea while on a six-week course of IV tigecycline for presumed left stump osteomyelitis. Her gastrointestinal symptoms resolved after discontinuation of tigecycline, suggesting a medication side effect. She was transitioned to IV vancomycin and meropenem. Vascular surgery evaluated her left stump and recommended an above-knee amputation due to deep bone infection, which she agreed to schedule within two weeks. A urine culture grew Klebsiella oxytoca, sensitive to meropenem. Her PICC line was repositioned after imaging showed malposition. She remained stable, with controlled diabetes and improving infection markers, and was discharged home with plans for surgery and outpatient follow-up.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Tetracycline group causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
